title: Meridian task specification
description: The complete schema for one task specification (record_type: task-specification): a portable, human- and machine-readable statement of one concrete piece of work. A record declares THIS schema in its $schema, so a consumer that follows the declaration validates the whole record — the record envelope AND the specialised body — in one pass, and never accepts a record that is missing goal, initial_state, target_model or the other body fields. The record envelope is the SAME contract as registries/operating-model/scoped-record.schema.json (identity, scope, origin, authority): scripts/lib/task-specification.mjs validates every record against scoped-record.schema.json directly as well, so the canonical envelope check is reused and separately performed, never silently dropped. This schema narrows only what a task specification narrows: scope is restricted to the two workspace-scope-model areas a project task specification may occupy — project-workspace and repository-scope (user-profile and organization-profile hold rules and settings; run-state holds one execution run's episodic state, while a specification exists before any run and may drive several; built-in-methodology is Kernel methodology). It also adds the payload body: goal, an explicit initial_state, an explicit target_model, a reference to exactly one existing pattern in task-pattern-registry, a non-empty constraints list and a non-empty acceptance_criteria list whose items each carry a stable id, a statement and a structured verification (method plus expected_result) so that a free phrase with no checkable condition cannot satisfy a criterion. A task specification states the REQUIRED CONTENT of the work; it never carries run state (lifecycle stage, work status, current actor, transition history, next step) — that belongs to execution-state-model, a separate package. The rules this JSON Schema subset cannot state live in scripts/lib/task-specification.mjs: the declared $schema is RESOLVED as a LOGICAL address within the Meridian namespace, from the canonical logical base CANONICAL_RECORD_BASE (the logical address records/task-specification — not a filesystem directory, a repository or a storage mechanism; a storage adapter maps it onto an actual resource, and moving a record between storage mechanisms changes neither its id, scope, origin, authority nor the meaning of its $schema), and must resolve to exactly this file's logical address — not merely carry the right basename, and not the bare scoped-record envelope; task-pattern resolution against the built-in catalogue; work_kind / change_class agreement; portability of the body strings AND of the envelope reference strings (origin.source_ref, authority.authority_ref, authority.decision_ref) — no rooted machine path whatever separator precedes it and with no allow-list on the first segment (/@scope, /$private, /~service, an emoji, Cyrillic or CJK all count as rooted), while ordinary relative paths with scoped or $-prefixed segments are not flagged; no home-directory reference, no drive-letter path, no backslash path, no file URL; non-empty and non-duplicate criteria; run-state rejection; the Russian name. The contract is a mandatory part of the Kernel: an absent schema or absent fixtures is a validator FAIL, not an informational skip. The normative document is standards/workspace/task-specification.md.

scope_ref.description: The task specification's area. Only project-workspace and repository-scope are accepted; every other area of the workspace scope model is rejected here (and in scripts/lib/task-specification.mjs with the rationale). The envelope shape mirrors scoped-record.schema.json's scope_ref: repository-scope requires workspace_id, and organization_profile_id is accepted only on project-workspace.

origin.description: Same contract as scoped-record.schema.json's origin. A concrete specification is authored in a workspace, so kind 'built-in' is additionally rejected by scripts/lib/task-specification.mjs.

task_pattern_ref.description: A reference to exactly one pattern in task-pattern-registry. id is resolved against the built-in catalogue by scripts/lib/task-specification.mjs and fails on an unknown or ambiguous id. work_kind and change_class are optional; when present they must equal the resolved pattern's own classifier pair.

acceptance_criterion.description: One acceptance criterion. id is a stable semantic identifier, unique within the specification. statement is what must hold. verification is structured, not a free phrase: a method and the observable expected_result that counts as a pass.

payload.description: The body of one task specification. Closed: every field is required and no other field is accepted, so run-state fields (lifecycle_stage, work_status, current_actor, transition_history, next_action, …) are rejected here by construction.
